questions.prompt: What is the primary memory advantage of defining methods on a class prototype rather than inside the constructor?

options.text: Prototype methods run in Web Workers automatically.
Prototype methods exist as a single shared function in memory across all instances, rather than being re-created for each instance.
Prototype methods bypass garbage collection entirely.
Prototype methods can only be invoked asynchronously.

questions.explanation: Methods on the prototype are allocated once in memory. All instances delegate to this shared object, saving massive RAM.

questions.prompt: How are private class fields (e.g. #apiKey) enforced in modern JavaScript?

options.text: Through a naming convention that developers agree to respect.
By the V8 JavaScript engine itself at compile and runtime; attempting to access outside the class throws a SyntaxError.
By automatically converting the property into a symbol.
By freezing the object using Object.freeze().

questions.explanation: Native private fields (#) are hard private variables enforced directly by the JavaScript runtime engine.

questions.prompt: Why can bundlers tree-shake ES Modules (ESM) but cannot reliably tree-shake CommonJS (require)?

options.text: Because ESM imports and exports are static and can be analyzed at compile time, whereas CommonJS calls can be dynamic at runtime.
Because CommonJS is only supported in Linux environments.

questions.explanation: ESM structure is completely static (top-level only, fixed string specifiers). This allows static AST analysis to identify unused code before runtime.

questions.prompt: What is a detached DOM node in JavaScript?

options.text: A DOM element that has been removed from the visible HTML document but is still referenced by a JavaScript variable in memory.
A node created inside an iframe.
A custom HTML tag with a shadow root.

questions.explanation: Detached DOM nodes occur when elements are removed from the DOM tree, but JavaScript variables keep referencing them, preventing garbage collection.
